title: Rendering modes: SSR, SSG, ISR and client-only

videos.script:
The Vite planner sends the browser an empty page and a script, and draws everything after. The Nuxt planner sends the page already drawn. Today is about the difference, and about the other ways a page can be made. {{csr}} First what the Vite planner actually sends, and what that costs.

{{ssr}} Then rendering on the server, and hydration, the moment the browser's copy of Vue takes over the page it was sent. {{mismatch}} Then a bug that only exists because the page is drawn twice. At half past eleven at night in São Paulo, the server and the browser disagree about what day it is, and in production the page shows two todays.

{{ssg}} Then static generation, where every page is drawn once, at build time. {{rules}} Then route rules, a different mode for each page of one project, and a cache that serves a minute-old page on purpose.

{{client}} Then the fix for the two todays, by leaving to the browser what only the browser knows. {{choosing}} And last, how to choose, page by page.
